headline: Quiet body, quick clock — tempo and head movement carry the read.

sections.title: What lined up well
sections.body: The body positions measure clean: shoulder turn at the top (48.3°), X-factor (18.5°), hip rotation at impact (12.8°), spine tilt at address (25.4°), posture change (4.1°) and lateral weight shift (0.8%) all sit inside the typical tour bands.

sections.title: The main thing that stood out
sections.body: Your tempo measured 2.72 : 1 — noticeably quicker than the 3.1–3.7 range most tour swings show. The backswing takes less time relative to the downswing than the reference set.

sections.title: Also worth a look
sections.body: Your head moved sideways 44.2% of body scale during the swing, a bit past the typical 20–40% tour band.

sections.title: One we left out
sections.body: Lead-arm extension measured 131.0°, but wrist depth is unreliable from a single camera, so that number is low-confidence and wasn't factored into the read.
